title: Apps
lead: Connect the apps you already use. Each agent only sees the apps you give it, reading is fine, and anything that changes something asks you first.
none: Nothing connected yet. Pick an app below.

how.oauth: You'll sign in on {{name}}'s own page and press Allow. OpenDot never sees your password, and you can disconnect any time.
how.google: You'll sign in with Google and choose what to allow. OpenDot only asks for what this app needs.
how.open: Nothing to sign in to. It works right away.
how.key: Paste a key from your {{name}} settings. It's kept encrypted on this computer and never shown to the model.
how.local: This runs as a small program on this computer.
how.microsoft: You'll sign in to Microsoft with a short code and choose what to allow. Mail is drafts only: agents write, you send.
how.account: Type the account's user name and an app password. It's checked right away, then stored encrypted on this computer; the model never sees it.
how.link: Paste the link and you're done. Read only: agents can see your events but can't change them. Keep the link private, anyone who has it can read the calendar.

missing.node: This needs Node.js on this computer (nodejs.org). Install it, then come back.
missing.uv: This needs uv on this computer (docs.astral.sh/uv). Install it, then come back.

safety: Reading is allowed; adding, changing or sending things asks you first. You can change that per action later.
signInToast: 🔐 Finish signing in to {{name}} in the new window
confirmRemove: Disconnect {{name}}? Your agents won't be able to use it, and its sign-in is forgotten.

tools.title: What agents may do
tools.hint: Allow = just do it · Ask = check with you first · Never = not allowed.

google.title: Set up Google once
google.lead: Google only lets apps you register yourself use Gmail, Calendar and Drive. It takes about five minutes, once; after that each Google app is one tap.
google.https: Google only accepts sign-in addresses that are https:// or localhost. Do this step on the computer running OpenDot (at {{local}}), or through an https link.
google.privacy: Both stay encrypted on this computer. The client belongs to you, so no one else is involved.
google.tunnel: You opened OpenDot through a temporary link: it changes if the tunnel restarts. Signing in now works fine, and apps you've signed in keep working after it changes. Only a later sign-in would need the new link added here, or a fixed address: localhost on that computer (or through an SSH tunnel: ssh -L 7878:localhost:7878 your-server), or a Tailscale https link.
google.remote: Add the localhost address below as well as this one, so signing in also works from {{local}} on the computer running OpenDot.
google.mismatch: If Google says “redirect_uri_mismatch”: add {{addr}} to your Google client's Authorised redirect URIs (Google Cloud → Clients), then press Sign in again.
google.blocked: If Google says “Access blocked … Error 403: access_denied”: in Google Cloud → Google Auth Platform → Audience, add the Google account you're signing in with under Test users (or press Publish app).

custom.title: Add your own
custom.blurb: Any MCP server: a link, or a program on this computer.
custom.lead: For apps not in the list. If the link needs a sign-in, OpenDot will open it for you.
custom.name: Name
custom.tokenHint: Only if the app gave you one. Otherwise leave it empty.
custom.caution: Only add servers you trust: they see whatever your agents send them.

localOnly: {{name}} only allows signing in on the computer running OpenDot. Open http://localhost:7878 there and connect it from that screen.

microsoft.title: Set up Microsoft once
microsoft.lead: Microsoft needs an app registration of your own to let OpenDot read Outlook and OneDrive. It's free and takes a few minutes, once.
microsoft.privacy: Kept encrypted on this computer. There's no secret to paste.
